{{short description|Concept in Lagrangian mechanics}}

In [[analytical mechanics]] (particularly [[Lagrangian mechanics]]), '''generalized forces''' are conjugate to [[generalized coordinates]].  They are obtained from the applied [[force]]s {{math|1='''F'''{{sub|''i''}}, ''i'' = 1, …, ''n''}}, acting on a [[physical system|system]] that has its configuration defined in terms of generalized coordinates.  In the formulation of [[virtual work]], each generalized force is the coefficient of the variation of a generalized coordinate.

==Virtual work==
Generalized forces can be obtained from the computation of the [[virtual work]], {{mvar|δW}}, of the applied forces.<ref name="Torby1984">{{cite book |last=Torby |first=Bruce |title=Advanced Dynamics for Engineers |series=HRW Series in Mechanical Engineering |year=1984 |publisher=CBS College Publishing |location=United States of America |isbn=0-03-063366-4 |chapter=Energy Methods}}</ref>{{rp|265}}

The virtual work of the forces, {{math|'''F'''<sub>''i''</sub>}}, acting on the particles {{math|1=''P<sub>i</sub>'', ''i'' = 1, ..., ''n''}}, is given by
<math display="block">\delta W = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F_i \cdot \delta \mathbf r_i</math>
where {{math|''δ'''''r'''<sub>''i''</sub>}} is the [[virtual displacement]] of the particle {{mvar|P<sub>i</sub>}}.

===Generalized coordinates===
Let the position vectors of each of the particles, {{math|'''r'''<sub>''i''</sub>}}, be a function of the generalized coordinates, {{math|1=''q<sub>j</sub>'', ''j'' = 1, ..., ''m''}}.  Then the virtual displacements {{math|''δ'''''r'''<sub>''i''</sub>}} are given by
<math display="block">\delta \mathbf{r}_i = \sum_{j=1}^m \frac {\partial \mathbf {r}_i} {\partial q_j} \delta q_j,\quad i=1,\ldots, n,</math>
where {{mvar|δq<sub>j</sub>}} is the virtual displacement of the generalized coordinate {{mvar|q<sub>j</sub>}}.  

The virtual work for the system of particles becomes
<math display="block">\delta W = \mathbf F_1 \cdot \sum_{j=1}^m \frac {\partial \mathbf r_1} {\partial q_j} \delta q_j + \dots + \mathbf F_n \cdot \sum_{j=1}^m \frac {\partial \mathbf r_n} {\partial q_j} \delta q_j.</math>
Collect the coefficients of {{mvar|δq<sub>j</sub>}} so that
<math display="block">\delta W = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F_i \cdot \frac {\partial \mathbf r_i} {\partial q_1} \delta q_1 + \dots + \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F_i \cdot \frac {\partial \mathbf r_i} {\partial q_m} \delta q_m.</math>

===Generalized forces===
The virtual work of a system of particles can be written in the form
<math display="block"> \delta W = Q_1\delta q_1 + \dots + Q_m\delta q_m,</math>
where
<math display="block">Q_j = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F_i \cdot \frac {\partial \mathbf r_i} {\partial q_j},\quad j=1,\ldots, m,</math>
are called the generalized forces associated with the generalized coordinates {{math|1=''q<sub>j</sub>'', ''j'' = 1, ..., ''m''}}.

===Velocity formulation===
In the application of the principle of virtual work it is often convenient to obtain virtual displacements from the velocities of the system.  For the n particle system, let the velocity of each particle P<sub>i</sub> be {{math|'''V'''<sub>''i''</sub>}}, then the virtual displacement {{math|''δ'''''r'''<sub>''i''</sub>}} can also be written in the form<ref>T. R. Kane and D. A. Levinson, [https://www.amazon.com/Dynamics-Theory-Applications-Mechanical-Engineering/dp/0070378460 Dynamics, Theory and Applications], McGraw-Hill, NY, 2005.</ref>
<math display="block">\delta \mathbf r_i = \sum_{j=1}^m \frac {\partial \mathbf V_i} {\partial \dot q_j} \delta q_j,\quad i=1,\ldots, n.</math>

This means that the generalized force, {{mvar|Q<sub>j</sub>}}, can also be determined as
<math display="block">Q_j = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F_i \cdot \frac {\partial \mathbf V_i} {\partial \dot{q}_j}, \quad j=1,\ldots, m.</math>

==D'Alembert's principle==
D'Alembert formulated the dynamics of a particle as the equilibrium of the applied forces with an inertia force ([[apparent force]]), called [[D'Alembert's principle]].  The inertia force of a particle, {{mvar|P<sub>i</sub>}}, of mass {{mvar|m<sub>i</sub>}} is
<math display="block">\mathbf F_i^*=-m_i\mathbf A_i,\quad i=1,\ldots, n,</math>
where {{math|'''A'''<sub>''i''</sub>}} is the acceleration of the particle.

If the configuration of the particle system depends on the generalized coordinates {{math|1=''q<sub>j</sub>'', ''j'' = 1, ..., ''m''}}, then the generalized inertia force is given by
<math display="block">Q^*_j = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf F^*_{i} \cdot \frac {\partial \mathbf V_i} {\partial \dot q_j},\quad j=1,\ldots, m.</math>

D'Alembert's form of the principle of virtual work yields
<math display="block"> \delta W = (Q_1 + Q^*_1)\delta q_1 + \dots + (Q_m + Q^*_m)\delta q_m.</math>
